title: Absolute extrema and boundary analysis
section: Max/Min Problems ▷ Absolute Extrema on a Closed Region
terms: absolute maximum; absolute minimum; closed and bounded region; compact region; extreme value theorem; boundary critical point.

exposition.text:
A continuous function on a nonempty compact subset of Euclidean space attains its absolute
n
maximum and minimum. Closed and bounded subsets of R are compact. To locate extrema
on a region, examine interior stationary or nondifferentiable points and all boundary pieces,
including corners and endpoints.
A boundary restriction often reduces to a one-variable problem. Compare actual function values
at all candidates; classifying each interior point is unnecessary for this comparison. Without
compactness, extrema can fail to be attained even when a finite supremum or infimum exists.
The condition ∇f = 0 does not apply to every boundary extremum.

question.text:
What is the maximum of xy on x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, x + 2y ≤ 6?
9
(A) 3 (B) 4 (C) (D) 6 (E) 9
2

solution.text:
2
On the axes the value is zero. On the sloping edge, x = 6 − 2y, so xy = 6y − 2y , with maxi-
mum at y = 3/2, x = 3. The maximum is 9/2.

What is the minimum of x + y − 2x − 4y on 0 ≤ x, y ≤ 1?
(A) −5 (B) −4 (C) −3 (D) −2 (E) 0

solution.text:
2 2
Complete squares: f = (x − 1) + (y − 2) − 5. The point of the square closest to (1, 2) is
(1, 1), giving f = −4. The unconstrained stationary point (1, 2) is outside the region.

question.text:
2 2 2 2
On D = {(x, y) : 0 < x + y ≤ 1}, what can be said about f(x, y) = x + y ?
(A) It attains both minimum 0 and maximum 1.
(B) Its infimum is 0, not attained, and its maximum is 1.
(C) Its minimum is 1 and it has no maximum.
(D) Neither its infimum nor its supremum is finite.
(E) It attains a positive minimum smaller than 1.

solution.text:
The punctured disk omits the origin, so every value is positive but values tend to zero
along points approaching that omission. The infimum is zero and no minimum exists.
Boundary points with radius one attain the maximum one. Boundedness without closed-
ness does not guarantee both extrema.
